On Friday, May 21, 2021 at 9:33:48 AM UTC+2 sarah.j....@gmail.com wrote:
Hi everyone! 

A few months ago when I ran my code, I obtained better fit indices and never once experienced the following error code: 

lavaan WARNING: using a single label per parameter in a multiple group setting implies imposing equality constraints across all the groups; If this is not intended, either remove the label(s), or use a vector of labels (one for each group); See the Multiple groups section in the man page of model.syntax.lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negativelavaan WARNING: some estimated lv variances are negative

Now that I am revisiting my analyses - that message popped up and my fit indices tanked (CFI now = .875; CFI back then = .91)  

Below is my model code. 
My question is, has anyone experienced this? By chance is there a solution to this error message that may be worsening my fit indices?

NeighInflu=~1.0*PhysDis
NegPerCh=~1.0*Impul
NegPerCh=~1.0*Unemo
PeerInf=~1.0*PerDel

NeighInflu=~NeighInflu_Alc*Alc
NegPerCh=~NegPerCh_Alc*Alc
PeerInf=~PeerInf_Alc*Alc

Marij~Alc_Marij*Alc

NeighInflu~~VAR_NeighInflu*NeighInflu      
PhysDis~~VAR_PhysDis*PhysDis              

NegPerCh~~VAR_NegPerCh*NegPerCh            
Impul~~VAR_Impul*Impul                    
Unemo~~VAR_Unemo*Unemo                      

PeerInf~~VAR_PeerInf*PeerInf                
PerDel~~VAR_PerDel*PerDel              

Alc~~Var_Alc*Alc                     
Marij~~VAR_Marij*Marij               

NeighInflu~~NegPerCh
NeighInflu~~PeerInf
NegPerCh~~PeerInf

Marij~~Age
Alc~~Age

PhysDis~1;
Impul~1;
Unemo~1;
Alc~1;
Marij~1;
'
mymodel.6.fit<- cfa(mymodel.6,
                     data=project, 
                    group = "Race",
                    fixed.x=FALSE, estimator = "MLR", missing="FIML")

summary(mymodel.6.fit,
        rsquare=TRUE,
        standardized=TRUE,
        fit.measures=TRUE) 

fitmeasures(mymodel.6.fit, c("cfi", "rmsea","tli",estimator="MLR"))

Best, 
Sarah

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Error Message for Multigroup SEM analysis
parts:
Sarah

You need to have as many labels as groups you have, so 4 in your case
If you dont want to fix anything to be equal between groups, just dont add any labels, by default lavaan will estimate separate parameters for each group.
Use the labels to equate parameters between groups, always use all 4 labels, this way its easier to keep track of what is equated etc
